paragraphs: Ravina the Earlier. Rav Yosef responds to his words: so Semag, negative commandment 193, folio 63, beginning of column 3; likewise Tosafot, Hullin 48a, and Asheri, Ellu Terefot there. This is not the unqualified Ravina in the Talmud who was Rav Ashi's colleague—Rav Ashi was born on the day Rava died—since Rav Yosef comes to respond to his words: ‘Rav Yosef told him.’ Rosh writes: likewise in Ellu Metzi'ot 28a, ‘Ravina says: he announces a cloak; Rava says’—Ravina precedes Rava. Rav Ashi was born on the day Rava died, and Ravina was his pupil-colleague. End quotation. Rosh likewise writes this at the beginning of Ha-Nisrafin (see above, Rav Aha bar Rav). See below what I wrote there in Be'er Sheva's name. Heilprin quotes Asifat Zekenim (Bava Metzia 67a), naming a pupil of Rif. The checked Shittah Mekubbetzet instead reads “pupil of Rabbenu Peretz” [הר״ף] and gives part of the ensuing argument under a separate heading: ‘If you ask: Ravina contradicts Ravina, since above he said, “A mortgage without deduction,” etc.—some explain that there were two Ravinas: one in Rav Yosef's time, the one here; one in Rav Ashi's time, the one above. So it appears in Ellu Terefot, concerning “entangled in the flesh,” etc.: this Ravina is not the Ravina at the end of authoritative teaching. Rav Pappa was Rava's pupil, and Rav Kahana was Rava's pupil and Rav Ashi's teacher, as we say, “Rav Ashi said: when we were in Rav Kahana's house.” It is unreasonable that Rav Pappa should bring a practical ruling of Ravina, Rav Ashi's pupil-colleague. In Ellu Metzi'ot, “Ravina says: he announces a cloak; Rava says,” etc.; thus there was a Ravina older than Rava.’ End quotation. Our reading is ‘Abaye asked Rabbah: what of a mortgage?’ etc.; ‘Rav Pappi said: Ravina acted and extracted the produce, contrary to Rabbah bar Rav Huna’ (see there). In Oto Ve-Et Beno, Rav Ashi says, ‘When we were in Rav Pappi's house’ (see there). According to that reasoning, how could Rav Pappi bring a ruling of his pupil's pupil-colleague? At Yoma 78a, Ravina asks Rafram whether he accepts Rav Ashi’s statement. Tosafot Yeshanim compare the preceding report that Rav Rehumi saw Ravina crossing with the sandal worn as a garment. They suggest this may support two Ravinas. At the end of Nahalah Li-Yehoshua it is written: ‘Shittah Mekubbetzet, Beitzah 17a: Rav Yosef said, “The halakhah follows Rabbi, and as Ravina explains.” If you ask: Rav Yosef did not see Ravina—one may answer that there were two Ravinas. Alternatively, Rav Yosef did not say “as Ravina explains”; the Talmud's narrator says this: as Ravina explains.’ End quotation. For those in his generation, his teachers and pupils, see after Ravina the Later.
